messages:
Liam (Zenith): Hey team — onboarding integration hitting a lot of 429s during device warmup. Around 40-60% of installs see /v1/preflight 429s within the first minute after app start.

Aisha (CS): Thanks for the heads up @Liam. Can you share SDK version, platform, and a short timeline of what the client does on startup?

Liam (Zenith): SDK v1.4.2, mostly Android 11 fleet. Timeline: app starts -> background prefetch kicks for recommended content -> we call preflight for each active user/session. Happens when a push triggers many clients to wake. Sample header dump from a failing request:

```
GET /v1/preflight HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: Bearer ephem_abc123
User-Agent: ZenithMobile/3.2
Accept: application/json
Connection: keep-alive
x-client-region: us-west-1
x-device-id: device-xyz
```

Liam (Zenith): Server responds 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and no Retry-After header in some cases. Logs show a burst of identical preflight requests within <2s.

Ben (Eng): This looks like a classic ephemeral-token fanout + connection churn. Two quick checks: (1) are tokens minted per device on your auth server at the same time? (2) is the client reusing HTTP connections / enabling keepalive? If every device opens a fresh TLS handshake + fresh preflight, we saturate edge rate windows.

Liam (Zenith): Tokens are minted client-side on first run; many devices request tokens near simultaneously after push. We thought Cloudflare would smooth things but we still see local edge queuing.

Ben (Eng): Mitigations we recommend — client-side first: limit concurrency, serialize refreshes, add jitter/backoff. Server-side: we can enable preflight coalescing for your tenant for the onboarding window. Suggested client knobs: maxParallelPreflight=6, staggerJitter=random(0,3000) ms, and ensure Connection: keep-alive + http2 enabled. Example (pseudo-Android):

```
// limit concurrent preflight attempts
val preflightSemaphore = Semaphore(6)
fun preflightWithStagger(deviceId) {
  val jitter = Random.nextLong(0, 3000)
  delay(jitter)
  preflightSemaphore.withPermit {
    httpClient.newCall(preflightReq(deviceId)).execute()
  }
}

// serialize token refresh per device
val refreshLock = ConcurrentHashMap<String, Deferred<Token>>()
```

Ben (Eng): Also, make sure your token refresh flow checks for an inflight refresh and awaits it instead of kicking a new one — helps avoid N concurrent refreshes per device. Backoff: exponential with cap ~10s + jitter.

Aisha (CS): I'll file a temporary onboarding plan: if limiting concurrency doesn't clear the spike, we can request a tenant-side throttle bump and enable preflight coalescing for a 24–72 hour window. @Ben can roll the staging coalescing flag so we can test.

deploy-bot: Rolled out preflight-coalesce=true for tenant=zenith to staging at 2026-03-23T10:12:00Z. Monitor metrics: preflight_rate, preflight_429_count, handshake_time_ms.

Liam (Zenith): Trying client change now — enabling keepalive & capping concurrency. Will run a small cohort tomorrow morning and report. Any diagnostic headers we should capture?

Ben (Eng): Capture X-Edge-Node, TLS handshake time (client side), and a short request ID. If you can include x-device-id and x-client-region in logs that helps map to the edge. If 429s persist, paste a short trace with request ids and we'll enable deeper sampling.

Aisha (CS): Great. I'll sync with you after the cohort. If this fixes it, we'll add the suggested config to the onboarding playbook and update the SDK quickstart. :thumbsup: 

Liam (Zenith): Thanks all — patching now, will ping when the cohort run completes.

Ben (Eng): One more note — if your fleet uses aggressive DNS TTLs, that can concentrate connections to a single edge. If you can preferIPv4 in the SDK or increase DNS spread, that sometimes smooths TLS distribution across edges.

Liam (Zenith): Nice — hadn't thought of IPv4 preference. Will test that too. Cheers.
